audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Samuel 2 draft aligned to Hannah's song, priestly food extraction, reported sexual abuse, Samuel's growth, and oracle against Eli's house; later source/witness audit required.
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Hebrew-first naming, restored/mystical separation, narrative ambiguity, institutional power, vulnerable persons, violence, and misuse risks.

verses.restored: Hannah prayed and said: My heart exults in YHWH; my horn is raised in YHWH. My mouth opens wide over my enemies, because I rejoice in your deliverance.

familiar.text: And Hannah prayed, and said, My heart rejoiceth in the LORD, mine horn is exalted in the LORD: my mouth is enlarged over mine enemies; because I rejoice in thy salvation.

verses.restored: There is none holy like YHWH, for there is none besides you, and there is no rock like our God.

familiar.text: There is none holy as the LORD: for there is none beside thee: neither is there any rock like our God.

verses.restored: Do not multiply speaking so proudly, proudly; let arrogance not come out from your mouth. For a God of knowledge is YHWH, and by him deeds are weighed.

familiar.text: Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the LORD is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.

verses.restored: Bows of mighty ones are shattered, while those who stumble gird on strength.

familiar.text: The bows of the mighty men are broken, and they that stumbled are girded with strength.

verses.restored: Those who were full hire themselves out for bread, while hungry ones cease from hunger. Even the barren one bears seven, while she with many children languishes.

familiar.text: They that were full have hired out themselves for bread; and they that were hungry ceased: so that the barren hath born seven; and she that hath many children is waxed feeble.

verses.restored: YHWH puts to death and makes alive; he brings down to Sheol and raises up.

familiar.text: The LORD killeth, and maketh alive: he bringeth down to the grave, and bringeth up.

verses.restored: YHWH makes poor and makes rich; he brings low, also lifts up.

familiar.text: The LORD maketh poor, and maketh rich: he bringeth low, and lifteth up.

verses.restored: He raises the poor from dust; from ash heap he lifts the needy, to seat them with nobles and make them inherit a throne of honor. For pillars of earth belong to YHWH, and he sets the world upon them.

familiar.text: He raiseth up the poor out of the dust, and lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill, to set them among princes, and to make them inherit the throne of glory: for the pillars of the earth are the LORD’s, and he hath set the world upon them.

verses.restored: Feet of his faithful ones he guards, but wicked ones are silenced in darkness, for not by strength does a human prevail.

familiar.text: He will keep the feet of his saints, and the wicked shall be silent in darkness; for by strength shall no man prevail.

verses.restored: Those contending with YHWH are shattered; against them he thunders in heavens. YHWH judges ends of earth; he gives strength to his king and raises horn of his anointed.

familiar.text: The adversaries of the LORD shall be broken to pieces; out of heaven shall he thunder upon them: the LORD shall judge the ends of the earth; and he shall give strength unto his king, and exalt the horn of his anointed.

verses.restored: Elkanah went to Ramah, to his house. The boy was ministering to YHWH before Eli the priest.

familiar.text: And Elkanah went to Ramah to his house. And the child did minister unto the LORD before Eli the priest.

verses.restored: Now sons of Eli were sons of worthlessness; they did not know YHWH.

familiar.text: Now the sons of Eli were sons of Belial; they knew not the LORD.

verses.restored: The custom of priests with the people was this: whenever any human sacrificed a sacrifice, servant of priest came while meat was boiling, with a three-pronged fork in his hand.

familiar.text: And the priests’ custom with the people was, that, when any man offered sacrifice, the priest’s servant came, while the flesh was in seething, with a fleshhook of three teeth in his hand;

verses.restored: He thrust it into basin, kettle, cauldron, or pot. Everything the fork brought up, priest took for himself. Thus they did in Shiloh to all Israel who came there.

familiar.text: And he struck it into the pan, or kettle, or caldron, or pot; all that the fleshhook brought up the priest took for himself. So they did in Shiloh unto all the Israelites that came thither.

verses.restored: Even before they made fat smoke, servant of priest came and said to person sacrificing, Give meat to roast for priest, for he will not take boiled meat from you, but raw.

familiar.text: Also before they burnt the fat, the priest’s servant came, and said to the man that sacrificed, Give flesh to roast for the priest; for he will not have sodden flesh of thee, but raw.

verses.restored: If the person said to him, Let them first make fat smoke, then take for yourself as your soul desires, he would say, No, but you shall give now; and if not, I will take by force.

familiar.text: And if any man said unto him, Let them not fail to burn the fat presently, and then take as much as thy soul desireth; then he would answer him, Nay; but thou shalt give it me now: and if not, I will take it by force.

verses.restored: Sin of young men was very great before face of YHWH, because the men treated offering of YHWH with contempt.

familiar.text: Wherefore the sin of the young men was very great before the LORD: for men abhorred the offering of the LORD.

verses.restored: Samuel was ministering before face of YHWH, a boy girded with a linen ephod.

familiar.text: But Samuel ministered before the LORD, being a child, girded with a linen ephod.

verses.restored: His mother would make for him a small robe and bring it up to him from days to days, when she came up with her husband to sacrifice sacrifice of days.

familiar.text: Moreover his mother made him a little coat, and brought it to him from year to year, when she came up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice.

verses.restored: Eli blessed Elkanah and his wife and said, May YHWH establish offspring for you from this woman in place of petition/lent one who was asked for YHWH. Then they went to his place.

familiar.text: And Eli blessed Elkanah and his wife, and said, The LORD give thee seed of this woman for the loan which is lent to the LORD. And they went unto their own home.

verses.restored: YHWH attended Hannah, and she conceived and bore three sons and two daughters. The boy Samuel grew with YHWH.

familiar.text: And the LORD visited Hannah, so that she conceived, and bare three sons and two daughters. And the child Samuel grew before the LORD.

verses.restored: Eli was very old, and he heard all that his sons were doing to all Israel, and how they lay with women who served at entrance of tent of meeting.

familiar.text: Now Eli was very old, and heard all that his sons did unto all Israel; and how they lay with the women that assembled at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation.

verses.restored: He said to them, Why do you do things like these? For I hear of your evil deeds from all this people.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, Why do ye such things? for I hear of your evil dealings by all this people.

verses.restored: No, my sons, for report that I hear is not good, causing people of YHWH to transgress.

familiar.text: Nay, my sons; for it is no good report that I hear: ye make the LORD’s people to transgress.

verses.restored: If a human sins against a human, God may mediate for him; but if a human sins against YHWH, who can intercede for him? But they did not listen to voice of their father, for YHWH desired to put them to death.

familiar.text: If one man sin against another, the judge shall judge him: but if a man sin against the LORD, who shall intreat for him? Notwithstanding they hearkened not unto the voice of their father, because the LORD would slay them.

verses.restored: The boy Samuel continued growing in stature and in goodness with YHWH and also with humans.

familiar.text: And the child Samuel grew on, and was in favour both with the LORD, and also with men.

verses.restored: A man of God came to Eli and said to him, Thus says YHWH: Did I not reveal myself to house of your father when they were in Egypt under house of Pharaoh?

familiar.text: And there came a man of God unto Eli, and said unto him, Thus saith the LORD, Did I plainly appear unto the house of thy father, when they were in Egypt in Pharaoh’s house?

verses.restored: I chose him from all tribes of Israel for myself as priest, to go up upon my altar, to make incense smoke, to bear ephod before me. I gave to house of your father all fire offerings of children of Israel.

familiar.text: And did I choose him out of all the tribes of Israel to be my priest, to offer upon mine altar, to burn incense, to wear an ephod before me? and did I give unto the house of thy father all the offerings made by fire of the children of Israel?

verses.restored: Why do you kick at my sacrifice and at my offering that I commanded in dwelling, and honor your sons above me, making yourselves fat from first of every offering of Israel my people?

familiar.text: Wherefore kick ye at my sacrifice and at mine offering, which I have commanded in my habitation; and honourest thy sons above me, to make yourselves fat with the chiefest of all the offerings of Israel my people?

verses.restored: Therefore declaration of YHWH, God of Israel: I indeed said your house and house of your father would walk before me perpetually. But now, declaration of YHWH, far be it from me. For those honoring me I honor, and those despising me will be lightly regarded.

familiar.text: Wherefore the LORD God of Israel saith, I said indeed that thy house, and the house of thy father, should walk before me for ever: but now the LORD saith, Be it far from me; for them that honour me I will honour, and they that despise me shall be lightly esteemed.

verses.restored: Look, days are coming when I will cut off your arm and arm of house of your father, so that there will not be an elder in your house.

familiar.text: Behold, the days come, that I will cut off thine arm, and the arm of thy father’s house, that there shall not be an old man in thine house.

verses.restored: You will look upon distress of dwelling amid all good done to Israel, and there will not be an elder in your house all days.

familiar.text: And thou shalt see an enemy in my habitation, in all the wealth which God shall give Israel: and there shall not be an old man in thine house for ever.

verses.restored: Yet a man of yours I will not cut off from my altar, to consume your eyes and make your soul grieve; and all increase of your house will die as humans.

familiar.text: And the man of thine, whom I shall not cut off from mine altar, shall be to consume thine eyes, and to grieve thine heart: and all the increase of thine house shall die in the flower of their age.

verses.restored: This is sign for you that will come upon your two sons, upon Hophni and Phinehas: in one day both of them will die.

familiar.text: And this shall be a sign unto thee, that shall come upon thy two sons, on Hophni and Phinehas; in one day they shall die both of them.

verses.restored: I will raise for myself a faithful priest; according to what is in my heart and in my soul he will do. I will build for him a faithful house, and he will walk before my anointed all days.

familiar.text: And I will raise me up a faithful priest, that shall do according to that which is in mine heart and in my mind: and I will build him a sure house; and he shall walk before mine anointed for ever.

verses.restored: Everyone left in your house will come to bow down to him for a piece of silver and a loaf of bread, and will say, Please attach me to one of priestly offices so I may eat a morsel of bread.

familiar.text: And it shall come to pass, that every one that is left in thine house shall come and crouch to him for a piece of silver and a morsel of bread, and shall say, Put me, I pray thee, into one of the priests’ offices, that I may eat a piece of bread.

translation_notes: Hannah's song speaks from reversal of humiliation into public theological poetry. It must not be reduced to a fertility testimony or used to promise pregnancy.
Warrior, death, Sheol, poverty, wealth, and judgment imagery are poetic theology, not instructions for harming enemies or blaming impoverished and bereaved people.
Verse 5's 'barren one bears seven' is a reversal image. Fertility is not a measure of holiness, and people with many children are not divinely rejected.
The song's king and anointed references may be literary anticipation or later shaping; they do not sanctify monarchy or erase the anti-monarchical warning of 1 Samuel 8.
Hophni and Phinehas use priestly office to seize food through threat. This is economic and religious abuse, not merely bad manners or ritual technicality.
Verses 13-16 preserve contested priestly portions and fat-burning order; later audit should compare Torah traditions and textual witnesses.
Threatening to take offerings by force shows institutional coercion. Worshipers' compliance cannot be assumed to be consent.

Verse 22 reports that Eli heard his sons lay with women serving at the entrance. The women are not blamed; the passage concerns sexual exploitation or abuse under priestly power, and textual witnesses require audit.
Eli's verbal rebuke is inadequate accountability. Leaders who know of abuse must protect victims, remove access, report wrongdoing where appropriate, and not preserve family power.
The statement that YHWH desired to put the sons to death is difficult theological narration. It cannot excuse institutional inaction, fatalism, execution, or violence against accused persons.
Samuel's growth alongside corruption does not imply that children should remain in unsafe religious environments.
The man of God's oracle condemns Eli for honoring sons above YHWH and benefiting from offerings. Family loyalty does not override survivor safety or justice.
Body-fat language in the oracle critiques enrichment from exploitation; it must not become fat-shaming or a claim that body size reveals morality.
Threats against descendants reflect ancient corporate-household judgment. They may not justify hereditary guilt, collective punishment, or stigmatizing families of offenders.
The faithful-priest promise is not permission for clerical superiority, dynastic replacement violence, or claims that one later religious community invalidates Judaism.
safety_note: Do not romanticize clerical abuse, minimize threats over offerings, blame women serving at the sanctuary, or treat Eli's verbal rebuke as sufficient protection. Do not use Divine-death language for vigilantism or fatalism. Do not fat-shame Eli or apply hereditary punishment to offenders' families. Hannah's song must not become fertility triumphalism or holy-war instruction.
